title: Global View - All Saints Day
audio: mp3/158. Global View - All Saints Day.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: And my name is Catherine and today we have an exciting lesson for everyone out there, very cultural.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们为每个人提供了一个令人兴奋的课程，非常有文化。

segments.en: Exactly, very closely related to our Halloween lesson that we had but on this occasion we're going to be looking at All Saints Day.
segments.zh: 确切地说，与我们上过的万圣节课程非常密切相关，但在这次我们将关注诸圣日。

segments.en: Alright, so this is a festival that's celebrated in many different countries and we're learning today about some of the ceremonies and practices in those countries that are very closely tied to those local cultures.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这是一个在许多不同国家庆祝的节日，我们今天正在了解那些与当地文化密切相关的国家的一些仪式和做法。

segments.en: Exactly, so we're going to learn a little bit about culture and at the same time we're going to learn some great words and phrases.
segments.zh: 没错，所以我们将学习一些关于文化的知识，同时我们将学习一些很棒的单词和短语。

segments.en: So let's get started with this dialogue for the first time.
segments.zh: 所以让我们第一次开始这个对话。

segments.en: The day of the dead has arrived.
segments.zh: 亡灵节到了。

segments.en: All souls day and all saints day.
segments.zh: 万灵节和诸圣节。

segments.en: Your neighbor is crazy.
segments.zh: 你的邻居疯了。

segments.en: Why is he screaming that?
segments.zh: 他为什么要这么尖叫？

segments.en: Because today is the first of November, the day of the dead.
segments.zh: 因为今天是十一月一日，亡灵节。

segments.en: Oh, that's right.
segments.zh: 哦，对了。

segments.en: This is a very special day among many cultures around the world, especially in Latin America.
segments.zh: 在世界各地的许多文化中，尤其是在拉丁美洲，这是一个非常特别的日子。

segments.en: Seriously?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: I thought it was just like any other day except for the fact that people visit the cemetery and remember their loved ones.
segments.zh: 我还以为除了去墓地悼念亲人之外，这天和其他日子没什么区别。

segments.en: Well that's just part of it.
segments.zh: 好吧，这只是其中的一部分。

segments.en: People across the world celebrate in different ways.
segments.zh: 世界各地的人们以不同的方式庆祝。

segments.en: In Mexico for example it's common to see people building private altars honoring the deceased, using sugar skulls, preparing the favorite foods and beverages of the departed and visiting graves with these as gifts.
segments.zh: 比如在墨西哥，人们常在家中设祭坛纪念亡者，摆上糖制骷髅头，准备逝者生前最喜欢的食物和饮料，再带着这些祭品去扫墓。

segments.en: In the Philippines the tombs are cleaned or repainted.
segments.zh: 在菲律宾，墓葬被清洗或重新粉刷。

segments.en: Candles are lit and flowers are offered.
segments.zh: 人们点燃蜡烛，献上鲜花。

segments.en: Entire families camp out in cemeteries and sometimes spend a night or two near the relative's tombs.
segments.zh: 整个家庭在墓地露营，有时在亲戚的坟墓附近度过一两个晚上。

segments.en: Whoa, that's scary.
segments.zh: 哇，这太可怕了。

segments.en: I don't know if I could do that.
segments.zh: 我不知道我能不能做到这一点。

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: We should fear the living, not the dead.
segments.zh: 我们应该敬畏生者，而不是死者。

segments.en: And we're back, so did you know about these traditions in the Philippines and in Mexico?
segments.zh: 我们回来了，你知道菲律宾和墨西哥的这些传统吗？

segments.en: I know about the Mexican ones because there's a lot of Mexicans where I come from in Chicago and they still celebrate these things.
segments.zh: 我知道墨西哥人，因为我来自芝加哥的地方有很多墨西哥人，他们仍然庆祝这些事情。

segments.en: But I didn't know about the Philippines so I found this really interesting.
segments.zh: 但我不了解菲律宾，所以我觉得这很有趣。

segments.en: Interesting, right?
segments.zh: 有趣，对吧？

segments.en: Actually, yeah, the Philippines as well as Mexico are very Catholic countries so maybe that's one of the reasons why they have these events that are so important for their culture.
segments.zh: 实际上，是的，菲律宾和墨西哥都是非常天主教的国家，所以这也许是他们举办这些对他们的文化如此重要的事件的原因之一。

segments.en: I'm sure, yeah.
segments.zh: 我确定，是的。

segments.en: All right, so before we start talking a little bit more about the culture, why don't we take a look at language takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以在我们开始更多地谈论文化之前，我们为什么不看看语言外卖。

segments.en: Language takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: All right, the first word is a very common word especially if you're a church-going person.
segments.zh: 好吧，第一个词是一个非常常见的词，特别是如果你是一个去教堂的人。

segments.en: The word is altar.
segments.zh: 这个词是祭坛。

segments.en: Okay, an altar.
segments.zh: 好吧，一个祭坛。

segments.en: An altar, it's a thing.
segments.zh: 一个祭坛，这是一个东西。

segments.en: It's a thing and an altar is usually found inside a church as you said, right?
segments.zh: 正如你所说，这是一个东西，祭坛通常是在教堂内找到的，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's like a...
segments.zh: 所以它就像一个...

segments.en: Table.
segments.zh: 表。

segments.en: It's like a table.
segments.zh: 这就像一张桌子。

segments.en: Or a counter.
segments.zh: 或一个计数器。

segments.en: So the altar in the church is where the priest does all of the stuff that he does during the mass.
segments.zh: 所以教堂里的祭坛是牧师在弥撒中做的所有事情的地方。

segments.en: It's where he prepares the bread and the wine and it's essentially a table, yeah.
segments.zh: 这是他准备面包和酒的地方，它本质上是一张桌子，是的。

segments.en: But you can build an altar for yourself in your garden, for example, right?
segments.zh: 例如，你可以在你的花园里为自己建造一个祭坛，对吧？

segments.en: And it doesn't have to do with the Catholic religion necessarily.
segments.zh: 它不一定与天主教有关。

segments.en: No, not necessarily.
segments.zh: 不，不一定。

segments.en: You could have an altar in a Greek pagan temple where you give offerings to a god or goddess.
segments.zh: 你可以在希腊异教寺庙中有一个祭坛，在那里你向神或女神献祭。

segments.en: So in this case, an altar is a special religious table where you perform certain religious rites or functions.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，祭坛是一个特殊的宗教桌子，你可以在其中进行某些宗教仪式或功能。

segments.en: Okay, very interesting.
segments.zh: 好，很有意思。

segments.en: All right, and so it's common in Mexico for people to build private altars honoring the deceased.
segments.zh: 好吧，在墨西哥，人们通常会建造纪念死者的私人祭坛。

segments.en: So what is this word, deceased?
segments.zh: 那么这个词是什么，死了？

segments.en: All right, deceased is a noun.
segments.zh: 好吧，死者是名词。

segments.en: It's a word that we use to call someone who's dead or departed.
segments.zh: 这是一个我们用来称呼死去或离去的人的词。

segments.en: So the deceased was named John Smith.
segments.zh: 所以死者被命名为约翰·史密斯。

segments.en: So it's like a more technical term of saying somebody is dead.
segments.zh: 所以这就像一个更专业的术语，说某人已经死了。

segments.en: Right, and it's something that you'll often read in the newspaper when they don't want to say the dead guy.
segments.zh: 是的，当他们不想说死人时，你经常在报纸上读到这件事。

segments.en: The deceased was a doctor and he is survived by three children.
segments.zh: 死者是一名医生，他留下了三个孩子。

segments.en: And so deceased is a way to describe a person in a nicer way.
segments.zh: 所以死者是一种以更好的方式描述一个人的方式。

segments.en: Right, very good, the deceased.
segments.zh: 对，很好，死者。

segments.en: And you mentioned another word that's very closely related to deceased, the departed.
segments.zh: 你提到了另一个与死者密切相关的词，即逝者。

segments.en: That's right, and this is actually a famous word because of a Martin Scorsese movie that came out about two years ago.
segments.zh: 没错，这实际上是一个著名的词，因为马丁·斯科塞斯的电影大约在两年前上映。

segments.en: And departed, you know the word to depart, to leave.
segments.zh: 离开了，你知道离开的话语，离开。

segments.en: A person that is a departed is someone who has left us.
segments.zh: 一个已故的人是离开我们的人。

segments.en: It's a dead person.
segments.zh: 这是一个死人。

segments.en: So you can say the deceased or the departed, which basically means the same thing as the dead guy or the dead person.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说死者或死者，这基本上与死人或死人的意思相同。

segments.en: Exactly, but again, it's much more polite.
segments.zh: 没错，但同样，它更有礼貌。

segments.en: It's something that we hear often at funerals or that we read in magazines.
segments.zh: 这是我们在葬礼上经常听到的，或者我们在杂志上读到的东西。

segments.en: Okay, so for example, All Saints Day is a way of honoring the departed.
segments.zh: 好吧，例如，万圣节是纪念死者的一种方式。

segments.en: Exactly, very nice sounding.
segments.zh: 没错，听起来很不错。

segments.en: Yeah, it sounds better.
segments.zh: 是的，听起来更好。

segments.en: All right, so talking a little bit more about the departed and the traditions, it says here that many Mexicans use sugar skulls or have sugar skulls during this festivity.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以多谈一些关于逝者和传统的信息，它在这里说许多墨西哥人在这次庆祝活动中使用糖头骨或有糖头骨。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So a skull is the bones from a person's head.
segments.zh: 所以头骨是人头上的骨头。

segments.en: And so you can often see these on, for example, pirate ships.
segments.zh: 因此，您经常可以在海盗船上看到这些。

segments.en: We say skull and crossbones.
segments.zh: 我们说头骨和交叉骨。

segments.en: And so it's the bones from a head and you have the bones underneath.
segments.zh: 所以它是头部的骨头，你有下面的骨头。

segments.en: It's a very popular image on Halloween because it's scary.
segments.zh: 这是万圣节中非常受欢迎的图像，因为它很可怕。

segments.en: But a skull is essentially the bones from a head.
segments.zh: 但头骨本质上是头部的骨头。

segments.en: So it's like a person's head without the skin, eyes, lips, everything.
segments.zh: 所以它就像一个人的头，没有皮肤、眼睛、嘴唇，一切。

segments.en: Right, it's scary because it has empty black spaces where the eyes are supposed to be and you can see all the teeth, but nothing else.
segments.zh: 是的，这很可怕，因为它有空的黑色空间，眼睛应该在，你可以看到所有的牙齿，但没有别的。

segments.en: What about the sugar skulls?
segments.zh: 糖头骨呢？

segments.en: What are these?
segments.zh: 这些是什么？

segments.en: They're skulls made of sugar.
segments.zh: 它们是由糖制成的头骨。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And so they look like skulls because there's no cheeks and there's no skin or eyes, but they're beautiful because the Mexicans in their tradition, they color the sugar.
segments.zh: 所以它们看起来像头骨，因为没有脸颊，也没有皮肤或眼睛，但它们很漂亮，因为在他们的传统中，墨西哥人会给糖上色。

segments.en: So you can have white skulls with this beautiful green and pink and red and blue decorations and you can eat them because they're made of sugar.
segments.zh: 因此，您可以拥有带有这种美丽的绿色和粉红色、红色和蓝色装饰的白色头骨，您可以吃它们，因为它们是由糖制成的。

segments.en: And so it's a special treat that people have in the Mexican tradition on the Day of the Dead.
segments.zh: 因此，这是人们在死亡之日在墨西哥传统中的一种特殊享受。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And one of the many traditions apart from sugar skulls and building private altars, they also visit the person's tomb, if possible, right?
segments.zh: 除了糖头骨和建造私人祭坛外，他们还参观了人的坟墓，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So a tomb is an important word.
segments.zh: 所以坟墓是一个重要的词。

segments.en: So what is a tomb?
segments.zh: 那么什么是坟墓？

segments.en: A tomb is a place where someone is buried.
segments.zh: 坟墓是一个人被埋葬的地方。

segments.en: It's a space or a place and it can be big or small, but it's essentially the resting place of a dead person.
segments.zh: 它是一个空间或一个地方，它可以是大的或小的，但它本质上是死者的安息之地。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a tomb, where the person is.
segments.zh: 所以一个坟墓，人在哪里。

segments.en: And actually on the tomb, you have the tombstone, right?
segments.zh: 实际上在坟墓上，你有墓碑，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And a tombstone is the same as a gravestone and it's a piece of rock on which you write the name and the birth date and the death date of the person that is buried there.
segments.zh: 墓碑与墓碑相同，它是一块岩石，您在上面写下埋葬者的姓名、出生日期和死亡日期。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So that's the tombstone.
segments.zh: 所以这就是墓碑。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So an interesting amount of words here on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以在语言外卖上有很多有趣的词。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to this dialogue again and we'll be right back with Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不再听一次对话，我们会立即回到 Flueny Builder。

segments.en: Your neighbor is crazy.
segments.zh: 你的邻居疯了。

segments.en: Why is he screaming that?
segments.zh: 他为什么要这么尖叫？

segments.en: Because today is the first of November, the Day of the Dead.
segments.zh: 因为今天是十一月的第一天，死者的日子。

segments.en: Oh, that's right.
segments.zh: 哦，对了。

segments.en: This is a very special day among many cultures around the world, especially in Latin America.
segments.zh: 在世界各地的许多文化中，尤其是在拉丁美洲，这是一个非常特别的日子。

segments.en: Seriously?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: I thought it was just like any other day, except for the fact that people visit the cemetery and remember their loved ones.
segments.zh: 我以为这就像其他任何一天一样，除了人们参观墓地并记住他们所爱的人。

segments.en: Well, that's just part of it.
segments.zh: 嗯，这只是其中的一部分。

segments.en: People across the world celebrate in different ways.
segments.zh: 世界各地的人们以不同的方式庆祝。

segments.en: In Mexico, for example, it's common to see people building private altars honoring the deceased, using sugar skulls, preparing the favorite foods and beverages of the departed and visiting graves with these as gifts.
segments.zh: 例如，在墨西哥，人们通常会看到人们使用糖头骨建造纪念死者的私人祭坛，准备死者最喜欢的食物和饮料，并用这些作为礼物参观坟墓。

segments.en: In the Philippines, the tombs are cleaned or repainted.
segments.zh: 在菲律宾，墓葬被清洗或重新粉刷。

segments.en: Candles are lit and flowers are offered.
segments.zh: 人们点燃蜡烛，献上鲜花。

segments.en: Entire families camp out in cemeteries and sometimes spend a night or two near the relatives' tombs.
segments.zh: 整个家庭在墓地露营，有时在亲戚的坟墓附近度过一两个晚上。

segments.en: Whoa, that's scary.
segments.zh: 哇，这太可怕了。

segments.en: I don't know if I could do that.
segments.zh: 我不知道我能不能做到这一点。

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: We should fear the living, not the dead.
segments.zh: 我们应该敬畏生者，而不是死者。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So why don't we look at three main phrases on Fluency Builder now?
segments.zh: 那么我们现在为什么不看看 Fluency Builder 上的三个主要短语呢？

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Well, the first phrase should be obvious by now because it is the name of the holiday we're talking about and the name is the Day of the Dead.
segments.zh: 好吧，第一个短语现在应该是显而易见的，因为它是我们正在谈论的假期的名称，名字是死者的日子。

segments.en: The Day of the Dead.
segments.zh: 死者的日子。

segments.en: So this is their day.
segments.zh: 所以这是他们的一天。

segments.en: It is and it's the Day of the Dead because it's the day in which people around the world celebrate the departed.
segments.zh: 这是死者的日子，因为它是世界各地人们庆祝死者的日子。

segments.en: It's when they talk about and remember people that they've loved who've died.
segments.zh: 当他们谈论并记住他们爱过的人时，他们就会死去。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So it's not really like a sad day, right?
segments.zh: 所以这不是一个悲伤的日子，对吧？

segments.en: It's more of a happy remembering them and honoring them and how much you miss them, but in a good way.
segments.zh: 更快乐地记住它们并尊重它们以及你多么想念它们，但以一种很好的方式。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And you're not actually going to hear this very often in reference to American culture because it's not something Americans do and English people don't do either.
segments.zh: 而且你实际上不会经常听到关于美国文化的听到这一点，因为这不是美国人做的事情，英国人也不会做。

segments.en: But people, when they're talking about their own families and traditions, will want to talk about this because in the Philippines or in Latin America, you have a very strong culture, like a very strong tradition of celebrating this.
segments.zh: 但是人们，当他们谈论自己的家庭和传统时，会想谈论这一点，因为在菲律宾或拉丁美洲，你拥有非常强大的文化，就像庆祝这一点的非常强大的传统。

segments.en: So.
segments.zh: 那么。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And as we mentioned, this day is a day to honor or to remember your loved ones.
segments.zh: 正如我们所提到的，这一天是纪念或纪念您所爱之人的日子。

segments.en: And that's our second phrase, your loved ones.
segments.zh: 这是我们的第二句话，你所爱的人。

segments.en: The phrase loved ones might not be obvious to many people because you can love many people and many things, but loved ones is a phrase that generally means the people that you care about the most, your friends and your family.
segments.zh: 这句话对许多人来说可能不是显而易见的，因为你可以爱很多人和很多东西，但亲人通常意味着你最关心的人，你的朋友和你的家人。

segments.en: So you could say, I want to have a party, but I only want my loved ones to be there.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，我想开派对，但我只希望我所爱的人在那里。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Or he was in the hospital and all of his loved ones visited him.
segments.zh: 或者他在医院里，他所有的亲人都拜访了他。

segments.en: So all those people, not necessarily only family, it's friends and family that you love.
segments.zh: 所以所有这些人，不一定只是家人，你爱的是朋友和家人。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And so those are the people in the world that are the very closest to you.
segments.zh: 所以那些是世界上离你最近的人。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And our last phrase and probably one of the most interesting traditions that we were able to see in this dialogue is that people in the Philippines camp out in cemeteries on their family or loved ones tomb.
segments.zh: 我们的最后一句话，可能是我们在这次对话中看到的最有趣的传统之一，是菲律宾的人们在他们的家人或亲人的坟墓的墓地里露营。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So the phrase to camp out means to stay overnight to bring food and a tent or blankets.
segments.zh: 所以露营的短语意味着过夜带食物和帐篷或毯子。

segments.en: And it essentially means to make a camp so you can stay there.
segments.zh: 它本质上意味着扎营，这样你就可以留在那里。

segments.en: And this is very unusual to me because I can't imagine sleeping in a graveyard.
segments.zh: 这对我来说很不寻常，因为我无法想象睡在墓地里。

segments.en: I think I get the goosebumps.
segments.zh: 我想我会起鸡皮疙瘩。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So camp out or you can just say camp, right?
segments.zh: 所以露营，或者你可以说营地，对吧？

segments.en: You don't necessarily have to say both of them.
segments.zh: 你不一定要说他们两个。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: You can camp or you can camp out and camp out generally means that you're staying in a place that is temporary.
segments.zh: 你可以露营，也可以露营和露营，这通常意味着你住在一个暂时的地方。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So interesting phrases as well on Fluency Builder today.
segments.zh: 今天在 Fluency Builder 上也有如此有趣的短语。

segments.en: Let's listen to the dialogue for the last time and we'll be right back.
segments.zh: 让我们最后一次听对话，我们会马上回来的。

segments.en: The Day of the Dead has arrived.
segments.zh: 死者的日子已经到来。

segments.en: All souls day and all saints day.
segments.zh: 万灵节和诸圣节。

segments.en: Your neighbor is crazy.
segments.zh: 你的邻居疯了。

segments.en: Why is he screaming that?
segments.zh: 他为什么要这么尖叫？

segments.en: Because today is the first of November, the Day of the Dead.
segments.zh: 因为今天是十一月的第一天，死者的日子。

segments.en: Oh, that's right.
segments.zh: 哦，对了。

segments.en: This is a very special day among many cultures around the world, especially in Latin America.
segments.zh: 在世界各地的许多文化中，尤其是在拉丁美洲，这是一个非常特别的日子。

segments.en: Seriously?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: I thought it was just like any other day, except for the fact that people visit the cemetery and remember their loved ones.
segments.zh: 我以为这就像其他任何一天一样，除了人们参观墓地并记住他们所爱的人。

segments.en: Well, that's just part of it.
segments.zh: 嗯，这只是其中的一部分。

segments.en: People across the world celebrate in different ways.
segments.zh: 世界各地的人们以不同的方式庆祝。

segments.en: In Mexico, for example, it's common to see people building private altars honoring the deceased, using sugar skulls, preparing the favorite foods and beverages of the departed and visiting graves with these as gifts.
segments.zh: 例如，在墨西哥，人们通常会看到人们使用糖头骨建造纪念死者的私人祭坛，准备死者最喜欢的食物和饮料，并用这些作为礼物参观坟墓。

segments.en: In the Philippines, the tombs are cleaned or repainted.
segments.zh: 在菲律宾，墓葬被清洗或重新粉刷。

segments.en: Candles are lit and flowers are offered.
segments.zh: 人们点燃蜡烛，献上鲜花。

segments.en: Entire families camp out in cemeteries and sometimes spend a night or two near the relatives' tombs.
segments.zh: 整个家庭在墓地露营，有时在亲戚的坟墓附近度过一两个晚上。

segments.en: Oh, that's scary.
segments.zh: 哦，这很可怕。

segments.en: I don't know if I could do that.
segments.zh: 我不知道我能不能做到这一点。

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: We should fear the living, not the dead.
segments.zh: 我们应该敬畏生者，而不是死者。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So, Catherine, you mentioned that in Anglo-Saxon culture, England or in the United States, you don't have this type of tradition of honoring the dead or something like that, but you do visit the tomb of your loved ones or the cemetery as well, right?
segments.zh: 所以，凯瑟琳，你提到在盎格鲁-撒克逊文化、英国或美国，你没有这种尊重死者或类似的传统，但你也确实参观了你所爱的人的坟墓或墓地，对吧？

segments.en: People do, definitely.
segments.zh: 人们肯定会这样做。

segments.en: But you just don't have a national day where you do this.
segments.zh: 但你只是没有一个国庆日来做这件事。

segments.en: Well, Veterans Day is a day when we celebrate people who were killed in wars or people who participated in wars.
segments.zh: 好吧，退伍军人节是我们庆祝在战争中丧生的人或参与战争的人的日子。

segments.en: So in America, we have a day called Memorial Day in which we remember the people who have died serving the country in the military.
segments.zh: 所以在美国，我们有一个叫做阵亡将士纪念日的日子，我们纪念在军队中为国家服务的人。

segments.en: And so Memorial Day is a day in which many people like to go to the graveyards and to lay flowers or to remember the dead.
segments.zh: 所以阵亡将士纪念日是许多人喜欢去墓地献花或纪念死者的日子。

segments.en: But it really depends on your family.
segments.zh: 但这真的取决于你的家人。

segments.en: I mean, some people like to go the day a person died and on the anniversary or on a special day for them.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，有些人喜欢去一个人死去的那一天，在周年纪念日或对他们来说是一个特殊的日子。

segments.en: So it's very private and personal and individual.
segments.zh: 所以它是非常私密的、个人的和个人的。

segments.en: It's not something that we all do on one particular day.
segments.zh: 这不是我们在某一天都做的事情。

segments.en: And I think what may strike many people as different is that you visit the cemetery and if you ever have the chance to be in Mexico or in a Hispanic country, you will see that it's full of people and it's actually a, there's a lot of food and people are there eating on the tomb and just, and they've actually prepared the food that was the deceased's favorite.
segments.zh: 我认为可能让很多人感到不同的是，你参观了墓地，如果你有机会去墨西哥或西班牙裔国家，你会看到它到处都是人，实际上是一个，有很多食物，人们在坟墓上吃饭， 只是，他们实际上已经准备了死者最喜欢的食物。

segments.en: Wow, that's really nice though as a gesture because it's another way to remember the person and to celebrate how, how, like things that were happy for them.
segments.zh: 哇，虽然作为一种姿态真的很好，因为它是另一种方式来记住这个人，并庆祝如何、如何、喜欢让他们高兴的事情。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And it's a way of actually sharing a meal with that person even though that person isn't with you anymore in this world.
segments.zh: 即使那个人在这个世界上不再和你在一起，这也是一种与那个人分享一顿饭的方式。

segments.en: So yeah, it's actually very interesting.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，它实际上非常有趣。

segments.en: It goes back again to a little bit of the culture and the folklore and everything from different countries.
segments.zh: 它又回到了一点文化和民间传说以及来自不同国家的一切。

segments.en: And we want to know what you guys do or how you remember your deceased because each country has its own particular little very interesting way of doing it.
segments.zh: 我们想知道你们做了什么，或者你们如何记住自己的死者，因为每个国家都有自己特别有趣的方式。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So please share with us on our website EnglishPod.com your own traditions and the culture that you have in your home country or town.
segments.zh: 因此，请在我们的网站 englishpod.com 上与我们分享您自己的传统和您在本国或城镇的文化。

segments.en: And we're very curious to hear those.
segments.zh: 我们很想听到这些。

segments.en: But also if you have questions as always, please ask because we're happy to answer those.
segments.zh: 但是，如果您一如既往地有问题，请提问，因为我们很乐意回答这些问题。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 到时候见。

segments.en: Bye everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。

segments.en: Bye, bye.
segments.zh: 再见，再见。
